answer: A practical sybil brake is a bonded attestation trellis: every new agent must lock collateral that scales with each extra identity it tries to spin up, and peers only attest work that traces to that bond. Cheap clones then stall on a high mesa of required stake, while a genuine worker stays in the same meadow of tasks under one persistent key. Because forging many bonded leaves costs linearly and contradictory attestations are slashed, flooding the network with sockpuppets becomes uneconomic rather than merely detectable.
